questions.question: The word that must appear in a correct definition of drought is NORMAL, because:
options: Drought is rainfall well below the average a particular place usually receives and has built its life around — Springbok thrives on a total that would devastate Mbombela
All droughts deliver exactly the same rainfall total
Drought only occurs in places with low normal rainfall
Normal rainfall means 500 millimetres everywhere

questions.question: The four stages of drought in their correct deepening order are:
options: Hydrological, agricultural, meteorological, socio-economic
Meteorological, agricultural, hydrological, socio-economic
Socio-economic, hydrological, agricultural, meteorological
Agricultural, meteorological, socio-economic, hydrological

questions.question: Hydrological drought is reached when:
options: The first season of poor rain is recorded
Crops begin to wilt in the fields
The shortage reaches the storage system — rivers dwindle, dam levels slide and the water table sinks
Food prices begin to climb

questions.question: El Niño matters to southern African drought because:
options: It cools the eastern Pacific and floods our interior
It only affects the northern hemisphere
It strengthens the ITCZ over Zimbabwe
A warm eastern Pacific rearranges the global circulation so our summer rains usually shrink — as the 2023-24 event showed by scorching harvests across the region

questions.question: Desertification is best defined as:
options: Degradation of land in arid and semi-arid regions until it behaves like desert — mostly caused by human pressure, not by deserts advancing
The Sahara physically marching southward like a wall of dunes
Any period of low rainfall
The natural ageing of all soil

questions.question: Salinisation enters the causal chain through:
options: Overgrazing compacting the soil
Generous irrigation in hot climates — the water evaporates and leaves its salts behind until the whitened ground grows nothing
Wind carrying sea salt inland
Trees absorbing salt from the bedrock

questions.question: The desertification feedback spiral runs:
options: More vegetation, more rain, more soil
Less rain, more vegetation, less erosion
Bare soil crusts, rain sheets off cutting dongas and stripping topsoil, thinner soil regrows less cover, more ground is bared and erosion accelerates
Erosion deposits topsoil evenly, improving the land

questions.question: In South Africa the classic desertification symptoms appear in:
options: The Cape winelands only
The high-rainfall Drakensberg crest
The city centres of Gauteng
The Karoo margins, the Kalahari fringe and the crowded communal lands of the old Eastern Cape reserves

subtopics.title: Effects on People and the Environment

questions.question: Soil loss is counted among the most serious environmental effects because:
options: Soil that took around a thousand years to form can be stripped in a season and is not replaced on any human timescale
Soil can be re-manufactured within a year
Soil loss affects only river mouths
Wind never moves soil, only water does

questions.question: Drought migration refers to:
options: Livestock walking to new grazing
Rural families sending members to the cities as farm work and income dry up, swelling informal settlements
Birds leaving a drought region
Government relocating dams

questions.question: By the winter of 2022, Nelson Mandela Bay's combined supply dams had fallen to roughly:
options: Three-quarters of capacity
Half of capacity
One-tenth of capacity, with the large Kouga Dam among the worst affected
They remained completely full

questions.question: Among the emergency measures that kept Gqeberha's taps open were:
options: Closing all schools and factories permanently
Importing icebergs from the Southern Ocean
Abandoning the city's coastal suburbs
Throttling mains pressure, chasing leaks, drilling emergency boreholes, adding Orange River water via the Nooitgedagt scheme, and pushing residents toward fifty litres per person per day

questions.question: Early warning turns forecasts into farm decisions when farmers:
options: Destock early while animals still fetch a price, plant drought-tolerant crops and bank fodder in good seasons
Wait for the drought to peak before selling
Double their herds to compensate in advance
Ignore satellite veld indices as unreliable

questions.question: Agriculture is the priority target for water demand management because:
options: Farms use almost no water
It is the country's largest water consumer, so drip irrigation, night watering and mulching save more than any household measure
Households cannot reduce their use at all
Industry uses more water than farming

questions.question: Working for Water restores streamflow by:
options: Building desalination plants inland
Deepening every borehole in a catchment
Paying crews to clear water-hungry alien invaders such as wattle, pine and eucalyptus from catchments, creating rural jobs at the same time
Damming every river in the country

questions.question: The Great Green Wall is accurately described as:
options: A single unbroken forest planted in one project
A concrete barrier against the Sahara's dunes
A programme limited to Senegal
Thousands of village-led restoration projects — trees, grazing management, water harvesting — stitched across the Sahel from Senegal to Djibouti under one banner

questions.question: In the bundle picture, drought is:
options: This month's bundle loading at a fraction of what this particular account was built around — not simply a small bundle
Any account with a small monthly bundle
An account that never loads data
A bundle that loads twice in one month

questions.question: The order bundle, apps, reserves, life corresponds to:
options: Socio-economic, hydrological, agricultural, meteorological drought
Meteorological, agricultural, hydrological, socio-economic drought
Agricultural, hydrological, meteorological, socio-economic drought
Four names for the same single stage

questions.question: The stages always arrive in that order because:
options: Officials declare them alphabetically
Prices always fall before the rain does
The shortage physically works downward from the sky — rain first, then soil moisture, then rivers, dams and groundwater, then people's lives
Dams empty before the rain stops

questions.question: The goalmouth on a school sports field models desertification because:
options: Constant trampling kills the grass, the bared mud bakes hard, rain sheets off instead of soaking in, and the wind lifts the rest as dust
Goalposts poison the grass beneath them
Sports fields are always built on desert sand
Grass cannot grow where shadows fall

questions.question: Dongas are:
options: Windbreaks planted along contours
Gullies torn open by runoff racing across bared, crusted soil, bleeding the topsoil away
Salt pans left by irrigation
Terraces built to slow water on slopes

questions.question: The spiral 'has no brakes of its own' means:
options: It stops by itself after one season
Only heavy rain can halt it
Each round of soil loss regrows less cover, baring more ground for the next round — the damage feeds itself unless people intervene
It runs only during drought years

questions.question: The crowded communal lands of the old Eastern Cape reserves show severe degradation because:
options: They receive the least rainfall in the country
Their soils are naturally saline
Mining stripped their vegetation
History parked too many people and animals on too little land and left them no alternatives, forcing overgrazing and fuelwood cutting

questions.question: Nelson Mandela Bay's crisis was years in the making because:
options: Season after season from about 2015, the rains missed the Eastern Cape catchments that fill the metro's dams
A single flood destroyed the dams in 2022
The city deliberately drained its dams
The Orange River changed course

questions.question: Fifty litres per person per day is a striking target because:
options: It is more than most households normally use
One filled bath already exceeds it — daily life had to be redesigned around a bucket-scale budget
It applied only to swimming pools
It was never actually requested

questions.question: The three moves that organise any drought-management answer are:
options: Borrow, build, abandon
Predict, panic, pray
See it coming, spend less, heal the land
Dam, drain, desalinate

questions.question: A small percentage saving in agricultural water often beats a large household saving because:
options: Households cannot change their habits
Farm water is more expensive per litre
Cities have no water meters
Farming drinks most of the country's water, so the same percentage represents a far larger volume
